children: The auto component maker plans to expand its electric vehicle powertrain, seating, sunroof and advanced electronics businesses as it looks to capitalise on vehicle electrification and rising demand for premium features

Uno Minda is targeting nearly double its revenue to Rs 40,000 crore by financial year 2030, banking on electric vehicle (EV) powertrains, complete seating systems, sunroofs and advanced electronics to drive its next phase of growth. The auto component manufacturer plans to expand its product portfolio and manufacturing capabilities as automakers increase investments in electrification, technology and premium vehicle features. The company’s revenue stood at around Rs 19,700 crore in FY26, according to media reports. Its growth strategy reflects a broader shift in India’s automotive component industry, where suppliers are seeking to increase the value of components supplied per vehicle rather than relying solely on growth in vehicle production volumes.

Uno Minda is expanding its presence in electric-drive systems and other technology-intensive automotive components as manufacturers adapt to changing powertrain requirements. Its plans also cover seating systems, sunroofs and electronic features, which are gaining importance as passenger vehicles become more technologically advanced. The company’s expansion comes amid growing demand for EV-related components and increasing localisation of automotive technologies in India. It has also pursued technology partnerships and capacity additions to strengthen its position across conventional and electric vehicle platforms.

For FY27, Uno Minda has outlined capital expenditure of approximately Rs 1,750 crore, covering growth projects and investments required to maintain existing operations. Several manufacturing projects are expected to begin production or ramp up during the year, according to company updates. The strategy is aimed at diversifying revenue streams while strengthening its relationships with original equipment manufacturers (OEMs). Higher component value per vehicle, product innovation and export opportunities could support growth beyond overall vehicle sales.

The expansion also reflects the growing importance of premiumisation in India's passenger vehicle market. Features such as advanced lighting, infotainment systems, sunroofs and integrated seating solutions are becoming important areas of competition among automakers, creating opportunities for component suppliers. Industry analysts note that suppliers able to combine technology development, local manufacturing and product diversification may benefit from this shift. However, the pace of growth will depend on new plant utilisation, customer demand, project execution and the ability to manage rising input and labour costs.

The EV transition also presents a longer-term opportunity for component makers to move into higher-value products, including electric-drive units, controllers and related electronic systems. At the same time, capital-intensive expansion can put pressure on margins before new facilities reach optimal utilisation. For Uno Minda, achieving its FY30 revenue ambition will therefore depend not only on India's vehicle market expansion but also on converting investments and order wins into sustained sales. Its ability to scale newer businesses while maintaining profitability will remain a key factor in determining whether its technology-led growth strategy delivers the targeted results.
